implementation.name: Rust compiler
implementation.version_scope: Rust Book native executable workflow; the example uses rustc directly.

sources.label: Rust source licensing and component notices

fit.text: Native command-line executables; compiled output can run without the Rust compiler installed on the recipient's machine.

prerequisites.text: Learn ownership and moves alongside basic syntax; stack and heap lifetimes are part of the learning path.

execution.text: Compile hello.rs using rustc, then run the generated executable for the selected platform.

behavior.text: The compiler checks ownership rules; owned resources are dropped at the end of their scope. Ownership is not a garbage collector.

tooling.text: rustc compiles the example; rustfmt handles formatting and rust-analyzer supports editor integration.

maintenance.text: The compiled executable is platform-specific; keep compiler, dependencies and target platform in your deployment plan.

costs.text: Compiler distribution has source license choices; IDE products and support arrangements are separate decisions.

example.run_instructions: With Rust installed, run rustc hello.rs, then ./hello on Unix-like systems or .\hello.exe on Windows.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: Default source choice except files with their own notices; binary distributions include further component information.
licenses.notice: Read COPYRIGHT and the distribution's component notices before redistributing.
